title: Proportional KV slicing and OOM diffuser retry protocol
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:
When the serving runtime receives high-concurrency, long-context requests the KV working set can grow unpredictably and trigger OOMs on GPU. Existing eviction/fallback approaches are reactive and coarse-grained: full-eviction, model swap, or request rejection. This ticket designs and implements a proactive, proportional KV slicing mechanism plus an "OOM diffuser" retry protocol that smooths memory pressure across continuous batching windows while preserving token-level SLOs and correctness.

Goals:
- Prevent P99 OOM-induced request failures by diffusing memory pressure across requests and batches.
- Keep additional latency impact within SLO (target +<45ms median for affected requests).
- Provide deterministic, auditable fallbacks when memory pressure cannot be mitigated (quantized micro-models, partial-response with continuation token strategy).
- Minimize cost/regression surface vs current baseline.

Design overview (high-level):
1) Proportional KV slicing:
   - Each request's KV footprint is measured by active segment count and recency score (LRU age + token importance heuristic).
   - Under memory pressure we compute a proportional slice factor per request: slice_factor = clamp(1 - (overcommit_ratio * request_weight), min_slice, 1.0).
   - Slicing truncates KV segments beyond the slice boundary, preserving the most recent and high-importance keys.
   - Request weight factors in request TTL, explicit priority headers, and whether request originates from Dedicated/Private customers.

2) Diffuser retry protocol: a staged retry ladder to avoid immediate hard failures:
   - Stage A (soft degrade): reduce batch admission window and apply proportional slices to low-weight requests only; allow streaming partial responses and queue continuation tokens.
   - Stage B (micro-offload): opportunistically spill low-importance KV segments to host pinned memory or local NVMe (configurable) and continue serving at cost of higher CPU latency.
   - Stage C (model ladder): if memory still insufficient, transparently route selected requests to fallback model variants (quantized 4-bit or distilled small model) with per-request fidelity metadata in logs.
   - Stage D (reject w/ graceful fallback): last resort - return structured error with continuation handle and background retry scheduled by gateway.

3) Continuous-batching integration:
   - Admission controller monitors sliding-window free-GPU-memory and in-flight KV reservations.
   - When free memory dips below headroom threshold, admission controller reduces concurrent batch size and shortens batch latency horizon for low-priority lanes.
   - Batches are rebalanced: high-priority requests stay in fast lane; low-priority requests are elongated into longer windows where KV slicing can be deeper, or migrated to micro-offload.

4) Observability and safety signals:
   - New metrics: kv.slice_factor_histogram, kv.spill_bytes, diffuser.stage_duration_seconds, request.fidelity_tag, retry.success_after_stage.
   - Logs include deterministic decision traces for each degraded request (slice decisions, offload candidates, model fallback chosen).
   - Add audit events for any request that hits Stage C/D for enterprise compliance.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Proportional slicing preserves high-importance context while avoiding worst-case full-eviction; complexity increases in admission logic and KV bookkeeping.
- Micro-offload to host memory reduces OOM risk but increases tail latency—acceptable for best-effort lanes and Dedicated customers may opt-out.
- Model ladder preserves availability at cost of fidelity; must be surfaced via structured response metadata and telemetry to allow quality rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for slice calculation and slice application survive synthetic workload that previously triggered OOMs.
- E2E benchmark: under stress workload used to reproduce P99 OOMs, system reduces OOM failures by >=95% while median latency increase for affected requests <45ms and P95 <200ms for low-priority lane when micro-offload is used.
- Metrics and logs available in Console and generated traces for at least 30 days for rollout.
- Feature flag gated rollout with per-customer opt-out and runtime knobs for thresholds.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (design doc + perf model): finalize heuristics and slice math; prepare microbench harness (3d).
- M2 (kv manager + admission): implement slice_factor computation and admission controller hook; unit tests (7d).
- M3 (micro-offload path): implement pinned-host spill path and async restore; microbench + perf CI (10d).
- M4 (fallback model ladder): integrate routing to quantized micro-variants and structured response schema (5d).
- M5 (canary + metrics): rollout to canary pool with feature flag and full telemetry (5d).

Rollout plan:
- Dark launch slicing decisions in logs for 48 hours, compare to baseline (no action).
- Enable Stage A for 10% of traffic in canary; run for 72 hours.
- If stable, enable micro-offload Stage B on canary for 5% next week.
- Progressive increase with monitoring; Stage C/D only enabled for non-enterprise customers initially.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect slice heuristics could degrade important context: add deterministic A/B with golden prompt checks, adjust min_slice per model.
- Spill thrashing between host and GPU: implement cooldown watermark and async restore throttle.
- Observability blind spots: mandatory structured logs and a SLO alert when retry success after Stage B drops below 90%.

Open questions:
- Should Dedicated customers have a hard opt-in for micro-offload (preserve data locality)? Current proposal: opt-out via account flag.
- Exact weights for request importance (TTL vs priority header vs recency): we will iterate from conservative defaults and tune via canary telemetry.

Documentation/Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PROPORTIONAL+KV+SLICING+Design (internal)
- Perf harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/oom-harness/pull/148
- Initial benchmark dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/oom-diffuser-canary

- Create perf harness scenario that reproduces the OOM pattern in CI (owner: SRE on-call).
